label: <DEL> step, stronger when the sequence starts with v (or a)
explanation: 72% of activation mass falls on the delimiter step (t == L), where 8.5% of sequences fire (lift 8.6x). Whether and how strongly it fires there depends on the first original tokens: first token v gives a 66% firing rate and the top examples (near max) all start with v v or v; first token a, j, or d, or v in position 1, also raise it. Delimiter firing is more frequent for shorter L. The other ~25% of mass is on original-phase steps, mostly inputs g, o, x (first occurrence), at weak to moderate magnitude. It almost never fires in the copy phase (3.5% of mass) or at t=0/1. The predicate covers about half the mass. Precision is limited because many delimiter steps in v-initial sequences stay inactive (longer L), and recall is limited because of the graded first-token dependence and the original-phase g/o/x activations.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: v, a, j, d, i, m; least: x, 3, p, l) and the second original token (most: v, j, i, m, a, u; least: p, r, g, z); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=3, L=5 & t=4.
